architecture.llm_provider: Anthropic Claude (model id claude-sonnet-5 by default, via langchain-anthropic ChatAnthropic)
architecture.embedding_function: chromadb.utils.embedding_functions.DefaultEmbeddingFunction - local ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2, free, no API call
architecture.distance_metric: cosine (Chroma default for this embedding function)
architecture.chunking_strategy: Whole-document: one composite embedding per resume (skills + role + seniority + summary + full raw text). Resumes are short (1-2 pages) so no chunking needed. Identified upgrade path if precise skill-keyword recall proves insufficient: hybrid whole-doc + separate skills-only vector (reuses classifier's already-extracted skills list, no new LLM call). Section-based / recursive chunking were considered and rejected as not worth the added complexity for this document length.

memory_design.within_single_run: Annotated[List[...], add] reducers on state fields (raw_texts, parse_failures, classified) so loop iterations accumulate results instead of overwriting them
memory_design.short_term_thread_memory: MemorySaver checkpointer compiled into the graph; every API call gets a fresh thread_id - each request is an independent, inspectable thread
memory_design.long_term_cross_session_memory: Not implemented. LangGraph Store deferred until there is an actual user/session identity concept in the API
memory_design.query_conversational_context: Deliberately stateless - decided against session-based follow-up memory (e.g. 'now narrow to seniors') because there is no session/user concept in the API yet; if ever needed, the client should carry combined query context rather than the server maintaining conversation memory

folders.inbox: uploads/resume/ - newly uploaded, unprocessed files land here
folders.indexed: uploads/resume/indexed/ - moved here after successful classify + rename + index
folders.rejected: uploads/resume/rejected/ - moved here if file size > 2MB
folders.failed: uploads/resume/failed/ - moved here if parsing failed after retries exhausted
folders.note: This replaces the old data/resumes/ single-folder design from the first draft implementation

graph.framework: LangGraph StateGraph(GraphState), compiled with a MemorySaver checkpointer

nodes.name: scan_folder
nodes.role: Lists files currently sitting in the uploads/resume/ inbox. This is the loop's entry and re-entry point.

nodes.name: analyzer_agent
nodes.role: Checks the next file's size on disk against the 2MB cap.

nodes.name: ingestion_agent
nodes.role: Parses file text. First attempt uses pypdf; retry attempt falls back to pdfplumber (more tolerant of odd layouts).

nodes.name: classifier_agent
nodes.role: Extracts structured fields via Claude with_structured_output: skills, seniority, primary_role, summary, first_name, last_name, years_experience.

nodes.name: rename_agent
nodes.role: Renames the file to Firstname_Lastname_YearsExperience.ext, auto-incrementing a suffix on collision (_2, _3, ...), and moves it into indexed/.

nodes.name: indexer_agent
nodes.role: Builds the composite document text and upserts into Chroma, keyed by resume_id (UUID).

loops.name: parse-retry loop
loops.condition: route_after_ingestion: file still failing AND parse_retries < max_parse_retries (default 2)
loops.behavior: Switches PDF backend on retry (pypdf -> pdfplumber) rather than blindly repeating; only re-attempts files that are still failing, tracked via state["file_paths"] being overwritten to just the failures

loops.name: folder-drain loop
loops.edge: scan_folder -> analyzer_agent -> ... -> indexer_agent / rejected / failed -> back to scan_folder
loops.condition: route_has_work: inbox has files -> keep looping; inbox empty -> END
loops.behavior: Processes one file per iteration, moves it out of the inbox to indexed/rejected/failed, then re-scans - so files dropped in mid-run also get picked up, not just the files present when the loop started

routes.over_2mb: move to rejected/, loop back to scan_folder

routes.retries_exhausted: move to failed/, loop back to scan_folder

upload_branch.trigger_mechanism: Synchronous drain-on-upload. The POST /upload endpoint saves the incoming file(s) to the inbox, then invokes the graph starting at scan_folder, which drains the ENTIRE inbox (not just this call's files) before the HTTP response returns. This was chosen over a FastAPI background task or an independent scheduled poller because the loop mechanics inside the graph are identical regardless of trigger, this is the simplest to observe end-to-end, and switching to a background/scheduled trigger later requires only changing where resume_graph.invoke() is called from - not touching the graph itself.

nodes.name: query_guardrail_agent
nodes.llm: conditional - only on a keyword hit
nodes.role: Deterministic keyword screen against query_text using a plain comma-separated keyword file. Only if a keyword matches does it escalate to a single Claude judge call, which decides whether the match is a genuine problem (prompt injection attempt, or discriminatory/protected-class search intent such as age, gender, or disability-based filtering) versus a false positive (e.g. the word 'senior' as a legitimate job-title term). No keyword hit = skip the LLM entirely and pass straight through.

nodes.name: retrieval_agent
nodes.role: Queries Chroma for the top 20 results (n_results=20). Applies where_filter (e.g. seniority) on the first attempt.

nodes.name: synthesizer_agent
nodes.role: Writes a ranked prose summary of only the top 3-5 matches. The full list of up to 20 fetched results is still returned as structured data in the API response, separate from the narrated subset.

loops.name: broaden-search loop
loops.condition: route_after_retrieval: retrieved is empty AND broaden_attempts < max_broaden_attempts (default 2)
loops.behavior: First pass honors any where_filter (exact metadata match); the retry drops the filter and relies on semantic similarity alone

routes.reject: blocked response returned, no search performed

chroma_design.primary_key: resume_id - a UUID generated once in ingestion_agent at the moment a file is successfully parsed, then threaded unchanged through classifier_agent -> rename_agent -> indexer_agent. Never regenerated even if the file is renamed again later.
chroma_design.why_not_filename: Filename is mutable (rename_agent changes it, and can change it again on a future re-classification). Using it as the Chroma document ID would silently orphan the old entry on any rename instead of cleanly updating it, since Chroma upsert keys strictly by ID.

guardrails.scope_decision: Query-side only, not resume-document-side. Scanning every uploaded document with an LLM guardrail would be a real per-file cost at scale; the recruiter's query is small text, so checking it is cheap regardless of corpus size.
guardrails.mechanism: Two layers: (1) a deterministic keyword screen against a plain comma-separated keyword file - zero cost, always runs. (2) An LLM judge call, triggered ONLY on a keyword hit, deciding whether it's a genuine issue or a false positive.
guardrails.keyword_file_format: Plain comma-separated list (no category tagging) - user's explicit preference over category,keyword pairs.
catches: Prompt injection embedded in the query text
Discriminatory search intent (age / gender / disability / ethnicity-based filtering)
PII-fishing queries (asking directly for SSN/phone/address instead of searching by role or skill)
guardrails.explicitly_dropped: PII redaction on the synthesizer's answer text. Dropped because the recruiter downloads and reads the raw resume file directly anyway, so redacting the text summary doesn't meaningfully reduce PII exposure.

third_party_tools_considered_and_rejecte.presidio: Free, local, regex+NER based, no LLM call - good fit specifically for PII redaction, kept as a later option if that requirement ever returns
third_party_tools_considered_and_rejecte.guardrails_ai: Free library, but per-validator cost varies (some wrap an LLM call) - not needed for these two checks
third_party_tools_considered_and_rejecte.nemo_guardrails: Free library but architecturally built around LLM/embedding calls for its rails - heaviest option, not adopted

download_feature.implementation_note: Deliberately a plain FastAPI route, NOT a LangGraph node - a download has no judgment or branching to make, so wrapping it in the graph would be unnecessary ceremony
download_feature.logic: collection.get(ids=[resume_id]) to fetch metadata -> read stored_filename -> resolve path inside uploads/resume/indexed/ -> return FileResponse
download_feature.security_note: The client only ever sends an opaque UUID, never a filesystem path, which eliminates path-traversal risk entirely for this endpoint (unlike /upload, which must sanitize client-supplied filenames)

query_response_shape.answer_field: Narrative synthesis covering only the top 3-5 matches
query_response_shape.matches_field: Full list of up to 20 fetched results, meant for the UI to render as a scannable results table with clickable, downloadable names

resolved_edge_cases.rename_collision: Auto-increment suffix: John_Smith_5.pdf -> John_Smith_5_2.pdf -> John_Smith_5_3.pdf, etc.
resolved_edge_cases.oversized_file_in_a_batch: Rejected per-file, not per-batch - one oversized file doesn't block the other files uploaded alongside it
resolved_edge_cases.parse_failure_after_retries_exhausted: Moved to failed/, doesn't block other files in the same batch
resolved_edge_cases.pagination: Not implemented - top 20 fetched once and returned as a single list. Chroma has no native server-side cursor/offset for vector queries, so true pagination would mean over-fetching and slicing in-memory; decided not worth building until there's evidence recruiters need to look past the top 20 semantic matches

security_fixes_already_applied_in_curren: Path traversal fix on POST /upload: Path(f.filename).name strips any directory components from the client-supplied filename, plus a resolved-path containment check against resume_dir
Extension whitelist on POST /upload: only .pdf, .docx, .txt accepted
